column1: # The hard-case set: programs the engine is supposed to judge a particular way.
# One case = one small program + the rule it is about + the verdict the program
# deserves + whether the engine gets it right today.
# The judge runs each program with ONLY the named checker, counts the findings
# of the named rule, and compares the count with `expect`.
# The optional seventh column names a YAML file next to the program: the case
# is judged under that configuration instead of the defaults. A case that needs
# the project's own configuration -- a sanitizer the project declares, say --
# carries it, because a case judged under configuration it does not have would
# measure the wrong thing.
# `status` is the ratchet:
#   closed  the engine gets this right today, so it MUST keep getting it right
#   open    the engine gets this wrong today -- it is the work list
# The suite asserts every `closed` case still passes AND that the total score
# never falls below the floor recorded in HardCaseSuiteTest. So a fix cannot be
# paid for with a regression somewhere else.
# id                      checker                  rule                             expect       family     status
